text: The investigators looked back through clinic charts and then contacted treated patients. text: The patients had different suspected causes of knee pain, and imaging was not available for everyone. The discussion identifies this variation as a limitation. text: Follow-up relied on telephone reports about pain, mobility, exercise tolerance, climbing stairs, sleep, and adverse events. text: The clinic initially used BPC-157 with thymosin beta-4 and later used BPC-157 alone. text: Some patients had imaging before treatment, but the reported follow-up did not establish repair with post-treatment imaging. The authors call for future studies of structural changes. text: Patients were asked about adverse events during follow-up, and the discussion reports that none were noted. That reporting method describes what was recalled and recorded in this series. text: Steroid injections and platelet-rich plasma are discussed using other research, but neither was a concurrent comparison group in this study. text: The methods describe a retrospective chart review at a clinic, followed by assessment of patients who had already received the procedure. text: The treatment was delivered through an endoscopic procedure into the bladder wall. That preparation and route are central to what was observed. text: The experiment used healthy young male rats with surgically transected and repaired Achilles tendons. Treatments were given by the intraperitoneal route.
